facts.statement: The study reviewed records from 17 children and teenagers who had brain tumors called craniopharyngiomas and hormone problems, most of whom had surgery and radiation.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers looked at how these young patients learned and remembered spoken words, including how their performance changed over repeated attempts.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The group showed weaknesses in learning and remembering words, even though their overall intelligence and daily skills were considered average.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Patients who had trouble sleeping had worse problems with learning and memory than those without sleep issues.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In 75% of the patients, their ability to learn new words stopped improving or got worse as they repeated the test.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Further analysis showed these patients had a harder time remembering words from the middle of a list compared to the beginning or end.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: There was a tendency for patients to remember words that were not on the list, although they were still able to group related words together.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results suggest that doctors should carefully check memory skills and work together to manage sleep problems in these children.
facts.subject: humans
